note: THE LEG RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1108).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, stated first because it is what separates it from
every other schema carrier in src/. The other schemas are read by a
validator and by nothing else: they describe a record the composing party
already knows the shape of. This one is read TWICE, and the second reader
is the point. `validateLegs` in src/compose.mjs reads the field set from
it, and the path-composition state of the Brief workflow table RENDERS it
into the judge's prompt. So the text the Model composes against and the
text the refusal enforces are one file and cannot disagree.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured on 2026-09-12 over the two live Briefs
(theses/calling-saved-permission-durable-leaves and
theses/legs-real-quality-matter-degree). No file declared the Leg's
fields or what they mean. The composer inferred the shape from
.claude/skills/brief/SKILL.md's prose, wrote a Candidates JSON, and
`validateLegs` checked it afterwards -- so the only Harness text carrying
what a field means was a refusal string, seen only when shape had already
failed. Claim cardinality drifted accordingly: the first Brief carried 1
to 3 claims per Leg, the second 4 to 6, with up to six claims from one
Strand in a single Leg.
IT CARRIES THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH TOO (kogaki#1147). The field
table below is about one Leg; `path_rules` is about the sequence -- the
Section grouping, the order `depends_on` may name, the uniqueness of an id,
the claim cardinality. Those were enforced in src/compose.mjs and stated
nowhere a composer reads, so a path satisfied them by chance or learned
them from a refusal that had already spent an attempt. The refusals now
read their text from that section, for the reason the field set is read
from this one.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. Every MUST of the
composition design stays judgment-class and is judged at path review. A
missing field is refused here; a weak rationale is not, and no description
below is ever matched against a value.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.

what_a_leg_is: A Leg is one move of the Reader Path: the smallest unit that takes the
reader from one state to another. `Leg = Input + State` -- the Input is
the material it stands on (its Strands), and the State is the Move it
binds, which is what names the kind of reader-state transition it makes.
A Leg with no Move has no defined transition type and is not a Leg.
The Leg's shape is the field table below; The Leg and the Move it binds is why `move` sits among its required fields.

leg_id.description: This Leg's own id, unique within the path. Other Legs address it through `depends_on`, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id.

materials.description: The Strands this Leg stands on, as LessonDisplayIDs (`L<n>`). A Leg with no material asserts nothing on anyone's behalf.

purpose.description: What this Leg is for in the path -- the work it does toward the adopted Thesis, in one or two sentences. A VERB ABOUT THE READER, carrying no proposition from the material: a purpose that could be true or false of the world is a claim in the wrong field.

reader_state_before.description: What the reader holds when this Leg begins. Judged at the specialization occasion against the Move's `requires`: a Leg's before-state must be a consistent specialization of what its Move demands.

reader_state_after.description: What the reader holds when this Leg ends. Judged against the Move's `effect` the same way. The two state fields are the Leg's transition, written as the reader's condition rather than as the writer's intent -- the reader's CONDITION afterwards, never a proposition about the world.

depends_on.description: The EARLIER Legs whose conclusions this Leg stands on, by `leg_id`. May be empty. An id that is not an earlier Leg is refused -- a dependency on a later Leg is a path that cannot be read in order. The ordering rule is a property of the whole path and is stated in `path_rules` below.

rationale.description: Why this Leg sits HERE, at this position, rather than earlier or later. The ORDER ARGUMENT, not a restatement of the purpose and not a claim the Leg asserts.

move.description: The Move library entry this Leg binds, by id. The Move IS the State component of a Leg, so the binding is required rather than encouraged. COMPOSE IT FROM `moves_you_may_bind` IN THIS ASK'S INPUT AND FROM NOTHING ELSE: that field carries every admitted Move with its `requires` and `effect`, and an id outside it resolves to no record and is refused at composition, naming the Leg and the id. The library grows by an admission act, never by a path naming an id (kogaki#1125).

claims.description: What this Leg ASSERTS, one entry per Strand it names in `materials`. A claim is a PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD and names no reader; a claim that mentions the reader belongs in `purpose` or in a state field. Its ground is the pinned Lesson, held as an address in the Brief's Strands section and never copied here. See `claim` below -- the cardinality rule is the part most likely to be got wrong.

journeys.description: The Journeys this Leg draws on, each naming the Strand whose Journey it takes and what the Leg uses it for. A Journey is MATERIAL THE LEG EDITS, never an assertion the Leg must recover -- it carries no claim, Reverse Outlining checks no fragment of it, and the Leg Packet renders it as prose to edit for the Move's purpose. Nothing here bounds how many a Leg declares: a Leg telling two cases for one claim is a path-review judgment, the way the number of claims is bounded by the Leg's materials rather than by a number. See `journey` below.

entailed.description: True where a proposition this Leg asserts is not explicit in the material and is reached by inference. The flag is the composer's judgment; the Harness refuses only a flag with no reasoning beside it.

entailment_reasoning.description: The inference itself, stated so path review and the owner can judge it. Entailment is interpretation, judged rather than silently trusted.

bridges.description: Present only on a Leg inserted between two adjacent Legs during the revise pass; names that adjacent pair by `leg_id`. It is disclosed at the Candidate-selection gate, so an unvalidated marking would render at an owner surface. The Bridge Leg and the revise pass is where that insertion is defined.

introduces.description: Terms this Leg introduces to the reader for the first time. The accumulated ledger the Leg Packet renders is derived from these; whether a term is genuinely new HERE is a judgment and is not checked. The reader-knowledge ledger is the accumulation this feeds.

opens_section.description: Present on a Leg that opens a Section of the finished article; carries that Section's name. The four grouping rules are a property of the WHOLE PATH and run after every Leg is known to be well formed -- they are stated in `path_rules` below, as the validator checks them, and three of the four refuse. The Section grouping carries the four rules.

figure.description: The composer's statement of what a figure lets the reader hold here that the prose leaves hard to hold. The default is NO figure: a Leg without this field has none and nothing asks about it. The figure decision is where the field is defined.

figure_roles.description: Binds every role of the Move's `visual_form` to one of THIS Leg's own claims, addressed `g<n>` and numbered from 1 in the order the claims are declared. A role bound to another Leg's claim is unreachable by construction: the address space is this Leg's claims and has no syntax for anyone else's.

relations.description: Which of this Leg's `claims` and `introduces` entries are SATELLITES, and of which NUCLEUS -- the relations layer (kogaki#1174). Every item this field does not name is a nucleus BY DEFAULT: the field marks subordination and nothing else, so a Leg composed before this field, or one carrying no satellite, renders exactly as it always did. See `relation` below for the address grammar and the closed relation set.

budget.description: The word bound this Leg's realized prose may spend, rendered in the Packet's write instruction. A LIMIT THE WRITER SEES, never a target to reach -- its absence means no bound is declared, and nothing asks about it.

note: THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH, AND WHY THEY ARE DECLARED HERE
(kogaki#1147). Everything above is a rule about ONE Leg, and a composer
was already shown it. The rules below are about the PATH -- a Leg's
relation to its neighbours, and the sequence taken as a whole -- and until
this issue they lived in code alone: `validateLegs` and
`sectionGroupingRefusal` in src/compose.mjs raised them, and the composing
party met one for the first time in a refusal that had already cost one of
its three attempts. Two runs on 2026-09-18 died at path composition on the
Section grouping's rule 4, each having satisfied every field-level rule it
was shown. A rule enforced over a record and never stated to the party
that composes it can be satisfied only by chance.
THE REFUSALS READ THEIR TEXT FROM THE ENTRIES BELOW, which is the same
arrangement the field table above already has: the prompt and the refusal
cannot disagree when there is one file. A rule stated here with no refusal
reading it, or a refusal composing its own wording, is the two-carrier
drift this file exists to remove -- and `checks/check-brief-compose.sh`
reads every refusal these two functions raise back against this section.
EACH ENTRY CARRIES `name` AND `rule`. The `name` is what the refusal says
first, so a refused composer can find the rule it broke by searching this
file for the words it was just handed; the `rule` is the rule as the
validator checks it. `class` is `checked` where a refusal enforces it and
`judgment` where it is yours to make -- a judgment-class rule is stated
HERE, beside the checked ones, because the two read alike to whoever
composes against them and only one of them will ever refuse. Nothing
below is matched against a value: a rule marked `judgment` is judged at
path review, and Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint is the
rule that keeps it there.
The Section grouping is where the four Section rules are ratified; the
Leg's shape carries the path's own order and the uniqueness of an id; the
claims rule carries the cardinality.

path_is_non_empty.name: the Leg's shape -- a path is an ordered sequence of Legs
path_is_non_empty.rule: A composed path is a NON-EMPTY, ORDERED array of Leg records, read in the order it is written.

leg_id_unique.name: the Leg's shape -- one id per Leg
leg_id_unique.rule: Each `leg_id` is unique within the path. Two Legs sharing an id leave every `depends_on` naming it ambiguous, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id, so it would address both at once.

depends_on_ordering.name: the Leg's shape -- depends_on names an EARLIER Leg
depends_on_ordering.rule: Every id in a Leg's `depends_on` names a Leg EARLIER in the path. An id that is not an earlier Leg -- a later one, or one no Leg carries -- is a path that cannot be read in order.

one_claim_per_strand.name: the claims rule -- one claim per Strand, per Leg
one_claim_per_strand.rule: A Leg asserts ONE claim on behalf of each Strand it names in `materials`. A Strand that serves several Legs carries a DIFFERENT claim in each -- that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement -- so the repair for a second claim is to move it to the Leg where the reader needs it, or to drop it, never to merge the two into a longer proposition.

section_rule_1.name: the Section grouping rule 1
section_rule_1.rule: A Leg OPENS a Section when it changes the reader's question -- its `purpose` answers a question the previous Leg did not pose, or its `introduces` names a term later Legs use. This is the positive case and it is YOURS TO JUDGE: nothing checks it, and its violation is exactly rule 2's refusal.

section_rule_2.name: the Section grouping rule 2
section_rule_2.rule: A Leg CONTINUES the current Section when it develops the previous one -- when its `depends_on` is exactly the immediately preceding Leg AND its `materials` overlap that Leg's. A Leg that develops its predecessor may not open a new Section.

section_rule_3.name: the Section grouping rule 3
section_rule_3.rule: The FIRST Leg of the path always opens a Section. A path that declares `opens_section` nowhere renders as one unbroken run of prose, which is the second of the two drafts the 2026-09-03 ruling rejected.

section_rule_4.name: the Section grouping rule 4
section_rule_4.rule: TWO ADJACENT SECTIONS HOLDING EXACTLY ONE LEG EACH are refused with a request to MERGE them, because a heading on every Leg is the first of the two drafts the ruling rejected. Length enters as a bound on the grouping, never as its reason.
section_rule_4.the_other_clause: Rule 4's other clause -- a Section running past roughly a display and a half of prose without a heading -- measures REALIZED PROSE, which no Brief contains. It is a named deferred slot in the Section grouping: it binds your judgment while you group the Legs, and no refusal reads it.

reader_start_binds_first_leg.name: Reader start binds the first Leg
reader_start_binds_first_leg.rule: The FIRST Leg's `reader_state_before` is the Brief's Reader start, verbatim. Reader start is the direction for the initial reader pull; a first Leg that begins somewhere else has the reader arriving at a Brief the article never opens from (kogaki#1151).

definition: A CLAIM IS THE ONE PROPOSITION THIS LEG ASSERTS ON BEHALF OF ONE
STRAND, FOR THIS READER AT THIS POINT IN THE PATH.
ITS GROUND IS THE PINNED LESSON, HELD AS AN ADDRESS AND NEVER COPIED.
In Toulmin's layout the claim is what is asserted and the ground is the
data it rests on; this field carries the assertion, and the Lesson it
rests on stays at its pin in the Brief's Strands section. The Lesson's
own Claim sentence is at that pin and is never rendered here or in the
Leg Packet, which is what keeps `assert nothing beyond` checkable:
what the Leg may assert is this list, and nothing arrives beside it.
A CLAIM IS A PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD AND NAMES NO READER. The
boundary against the Leg's other fields is one of grammatical kind:
`purpose` is a verb about the reader and carries no proposition from
the material, `reader_state_after` is the reader's condition
afterwards, and `rationale` is the order argument. A claim that
mentions the reader, or a purpose that could be true or false of the
world, is in the wrong field.
ONE CLAIM PER STRAND NAMED IN `materials`. Two claims in one Leg
naming the same Strand is REFUSED, naming the Leg and the Strand. A
Strand that serves several Legs carries a DIFFERENT claim in each --
that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement, and it
is why the rule is per Leg rather than per path.
WHY THE CARDINALITY IS BOUNDED AT ALL, measured rather than argued
(kogaki#1108). The Leg Packet requires every declared claim to be
recoverable from the realized passage, and `claims-unused` fails the
Leg otherwise. With cardinality unbounded, claim generation drifted
into composing the article's decisive lines wholesale and calling them
claims -- so the comparison the Packet performs stopped measuring
grounding and started measuring how much of the passage had been written
in advance. One proposition per Strand is what keeps a claim a claim
the Strand supports rather than a draft of the sentence that will carry
it.
A CLAIM IS ONE PROPOSITION DERIVED FROM A STRAND, AND NOTHING ELSE. The
type set is closed at `strand`. Inherited reader state belongs to
`reader_state_before` and to the computed `already knows` ledger; a
presupposed premise belongs to the Brief's Reader start. Neither is an
assertion, so a passage that realizes its Leg correctly never states
one and the Blind Reader never recovers it.
The claims rule is the spec half of this definition; the mechanical half -- the closed type set and the one-per-Strand refusal -- is carried here and enforced by `validateLegs`.

retired_types.leg_effect: inherited reader state, which is already carried by this Leg's `reader_state_before` and by the computed `already knows` ledger
retired_types.reader_assumption: a presupposed premise, which belongs to the Brief's Reader start

type.description: The closed set above. Today it has one member, `strand`.

proposition.description: The claim itself, STATED -- a specific proposition this Leg asserts, not a pointer at where one could be found. An untyped pointer is not a claim.

strand.description: The Strand this claim is asserted on behalf of, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Leg's `materials`, it is where the pinned Lesson that grounds the claim is addressed, and no other claim of this Leg names it.

definition: A JOURNEY IS MATERIAL THE LEG DRAWS ON, NEVER AN ASSERTION THE LEG
MUST RECOVER. A Lesson's Claim is a proposition, and the planning
decision is what transformation of it this Leg asserts -- so it is
carried in the Brief as the Leg's claim. A Journey is a narrative, and
how it is told depends on the Move being performed and on the prose
already on the page -- so it is ADDRESSED at planning and EDITED at
realization. That asymmetry is the whole of why this field carries an
address and a use rather than any text.
THE BRIEF CARRIES NO JOURNEY TEXT. The entry names a Strand and what
this Leg uses that Strand's Journey for; the prose lives at the
Strand's served journey cite, which the Brief already renders in its
Strands section. No decomposition of a Journey happens at planning
time.
IT ASSERTS NOTHING, AND THE CONSEQUENCES ARE MECHANICAL. A Journey
generates no claim, so `claims-unused` never asks for it back and the
Reverse Outline the Blind Reader hands over carries no Journey field
to compare. What this Leg may ASSERT is its `claims` list, and a
Journey placed here does not widen it.
THE USE IS FROM A CLOSED SET, in plain words, read from `uses` below.
It is what the Leg does with the material, not a claim about the
world: a use outside the set is refused by `validateLegs`, and
whether the use chosen serves the Move is path review's judgment.
COVERAGE ACCOUNTING IS TAKEN FROM THIS FIELD. Journey placement is
counted from `journeys`: a Strand's Journey is placed by a Leg when
that Leg declares an entry naming it here. It was once counted from a
`<L-id>.journey` token in `materials` instead, and that made two
readers of one fact -- a Leg that named its Strand bare and drew on
its Journey here rendered its `journey:` line and was disclosed as
OMITTED in the same Brief. A `<L-id>.journey` token stays legal, and
still names the Strand; it no longer places anything on its own.

uses.illustrate: to illustrate this Leg's claim with the concrete case the Journey tells
uses.motivate: to motivate the question this Leg opens, with the event that raised it
uses.contrast: to contrast, showing the expectation the event broke

strand.description: The Strand whose Journey this Leg draws on, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Leg's `materials` -- named bare or as `<L-id>.journey` -- and its served record must carry Journey material, which is what the Brief's `- journey cite:` line records.

use.description: What this Leg uses the Journey for, from the closed set in `uses` above. A use outside that set is refused.

definition: THE RELATIONS LAYER (kogaki#1174; owner ruling 2026-09-21). Without it,
every content item a Leg carries into the Packet -- its claims, its
`introduces` entries -- is a peer of every other one, with no relation
among them: the writer's only safe realization is one unit per item, in
the order given, and two items can never fuse into one sentence because
nothing says which is subordinate to which. That is what made a Closure
row a paragraph rather than a clause, and it is what this field removes.
A RELATION MARKS ONE ITEM A SATELLITE OF ANOTHER, NAMED, NUCLEUS. Every
item this Leg carries is a nucleus BY DEFAULT -- unmarked, a peer among
peers, exactly as before this field existed. Naming an item here as a
satellite is what subordinates it, and the writer realizes a satellite as
a clause or phrase attached to its nucleus, never as its own paragraph:
Reverse Outlining reads a satellite realized as a standalone paragraph as
a finding.
THE ADDRESS SPACE IS THIS LEG'S OWN ITEMS, and it is typed by kind: `g<n>`
addresses this Leg's nth declared CLAIM (the same address `figure_roles`
already uses), and `i<n>` addresses this Leg's nth declared `introduces`
entry, both 1-based in DECLARATION order. A satellite and its nucleus are
items of the SAME KIND -- a claim subordinates to a claim, an `introduces`
entry to an `introduces` entry -- because the two are rendered in separate
Packet blocks and a cross-kind tree would ask the renderer to move an item
out of the block its own heading promises it. Widening the address space
to reach across blocks is available later on its own licence.
THE CLOSURE LEDGER CARRIES NO RELATION MARKING HERE, and the omission is a
scoping decision rather than an oversight. A Closure row lives in the
Brief's OWN `obligations`/`thesis_closure` ledger (`fillBrief`), authored
at a different occasion than a Leg's own fields and addressed by no `g<n>`
or `i<n>` scheme -- folding it into this field would mean redesigning that
ledger's own shape, which is a wider act than this one licenses. A Closure
row renders exactly as it did before this field: a sibling, never a
satellite. Available later, on its own licence.
A TREE IS TWO LEVELS, NEVER A CHAIN. The nucleus a relation names must
itself be unmarked -- naming an item BOTH a satellite of one item and the
nucleus of another is refused, because the Packet renders one level of
indentation and a chain would ask the writer to read a level the block
never shows. Every item is a nucleus, or a satellite of one; nothing is
both.
ONE NUCLEUS PER SATELLITE, AND ONE ENTRY PER ITEM. An item named `item` in
two entries would leave the renderer choosing which relation to draw, so a
second entry naming the same item is refused rather than silently
overwriting the first.

types.background: the satellite supplies context the reader needs to place the nucleus, without which the nucleus is harder to locate
types.evidence: the satellite is what makes the reader believe the nucleus
types.elaboration: the satellite gives more detail of what the nucleus already asserts
types.concession: the satellite grants a point that might tell against the nucleus, before or after it stands
types.contrast: the satellite is juxtaposed against the nucleus to bring out a difference between them
types.cause: the satellite is why the nucleus is so
types.condition: the satellite states what must hold for the nucleus to hold
types.restatement: the satellite says the nucleus again, in other words

item.description: The satellite: the address of the item being subordinated, `g<n>` or `i<n>` over this Leg's own claims or `introduces` entries.

nucleus.description: The item `item` is a satellite OF, addressed the same way and of the SAME KIND as `item`. Must itself be unmarked -- a nucleus is not itself a satellite of anything (a tree is two levels, never a chain).

relation.description: The relation `item` bears to `nucleus`, from the closed set in `types` above. A relation type outside that set is refused.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether a rationale is good,
whether a claim is genuinely supported by its Strand, whether a term is
really introduced here, and whether the before/after states are faithful
specializations of the Move are all judgment-class: they are judged at
path review and at the specialization occasion, and a refusal from this
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule this paragraph is an instance of.
